editorial.headline: Roof Framing in Bali: Open Nationally and Outside the Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the specialised installation of building frames and roofs, from gutter work to roof painting, for residential and non-residential buildings.
editorial.body:
Roof framing and covering is a specialised building-construction activity with a clear practical centre: installing the structural frame and roof of residential and non-residential buildings. Its scope also includes gutter work and roof painting. In other words, it concerns the work that gives a building its overhead structure and finished protective covering, undertaken as part of wider building construction.

The activity is open to micro, small, medium and large enterprises. Nationally, it is open to PMA registration with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. That makes the national position unusually direct: foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership for this activity.

Bali requires a separate reading, because the province permanently blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk activities across the island. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the large-enterprise scale, its OSS risk classification is medium-high or high, placing it outside the moratorium’s stated reach. The Bali position is therefore not a hidden prohibition behind a nationally open classification: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today.

That conclusion rests on the activity’s stated Bali status and risk treatment, rather than on a general assumption about construction. The national setting permits up to full foreign ownership; Bali’s island-wide moratorium does not capture this activity because the relevant large-scale risk level is medium-high or high. For founders, the essential distinction is simple: the work is specialised roof-and-frame installation, it is available across every listed business scale, and its Bali position remains open rather than moratorium-blocked.
